2608.03512.title: Reversing Arrows in Large Language Models
2608.03512.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance on text-to-knowledge graph generation and related tasks. Nevertheless, it is still unclear whether they accurately model the direction-dependent semantics of inverse relations, in which reversing the order of the arguments alters the meaning of a relation (e.g., \textit{mother} versus \textit{child}). To the best of our knowledge, this work presents the first systematic study of inverse relation directionality in LLMs, using a benchmark consisting of 5,457 instances spanning 27 distinct inverse relation labels. We evaluate five open-source LLMs under a multiple-choice prompting framework and further examine the influence of relation descriptions and entity representations by substituting the original entities with synthetic and masked entities. Our findings reveal systematic asymmetries in inverse relation classification across LLMs, indicate that relation descriptions do not consistently improve performance, and show that model performance can be sensitive to variations in entity representations.
2608.03512.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在文本到知識圖譜生成及相關任務上已取得良好的表現。<lb/>然而，目前尚不清楚它們是否準確地建模了逆關係的方向依賴語義，在這種情況下，反轉參數的順序會改變關係的含義（例如，\textit{mother} 與 \textit{child}）。<lb/>據我們所知，本研究首次系統性地研究了LLMs中的逆關係方向性，使用了一個包含5,457個實例的基準，涵蓋27個不同的逆關係標籤。<lb/>我們在多選提示框架下評估了五個開源LLMs，並進一步通過用合成和遮蔽實體替換原始實體來檢查關係描述和實體表示的影響。<lb/>我們的研究結果揭示了LLMs在逆關係分類中的系統性不對稱，表明關係描述並不總是一致地提高性能，並顯示模型性能對實體表示的變化可能敏感。
2608.03512.author: Sefika Efeoglu et.al.
